# =============================================================================
# tessera-app-core: selection model and text extraction   (issue #30 part 1 of 3, wave 8)
# crates/tessera-app-core/tests/fixtures/selection_spec.txt
# spec-researcher output (2026-10-31). ONLY THE MILESTONE LEAD EDITS A FINALISED COPY. The implementer copies it
# verbatim and never edits a row: a row that looks wrong is REPORTED (row id, expected, actual, why) to the lead.
#
# STATUS: FINAL (2026-10-31, lead decisions recorded on #30). Companion files: selection_spec.notes.md (decisions,
# URL rules, schemes), hyperlink_spec.txt (tessera-term), selection_gestures.txt (Swift).
#
# ROW LAYOUT (same `###` layout as osc_spec.txt / wide_grapheme_spec.txt; tests/selection.rs needs its own parser)
#   ### <ID>
#   layer:   core            (App-level row; `url` rows are pure-function rows for url.rs and say so)
#   size:    <rows>x<cols>   screen size; `scrollback: <N>` optional history cap (default 100)
#   step:    one action per line, run in order:
#              feed <payload>                bytes into the terminal (escapes below)
#              begin R,C <char|word|line> [block]   App::select_begin at VIEW-relative (row,col), 0-based
#              extend R,C                    App::select_extend
#              all                           App::select_all
#              adjust R,C                    shift-click: move the endpoint NEARER to R,C (tie: the start), keeping granularity
#                                            and block-ness; no-op without a selection (NEW core call, see notes D5)
#              clear                         App::select_clear
#              link R,C                      App::link_at (checked by `link:`)
#              scroll N                      view scrolled N lines back into history (0 = live)
#              resize <rows>x<cols>
#              clear_scrollback              App::clear_scrollback
#   sel:     none | linear (R,C)-(R,C) | block (R,C)-(R,C)    the selection as the frame carries it AFTER the last
#            step: view-relative rows, both ends INCLUSIVE, normalised to reading order (linear) or to
#            top-left/bottom-right (block). Cells are reported AS CLICKED: a point on a wide character's SPACER or WIDE
#            half is NOT widened in `sel:`; extraction and the renderer widen it (REND). Rows outside the view are
#            clipped (`sel:` then lists the clipped part); a selection wholly outside the view is `sel: none` with
#            `has_selection: true`. Line granularity covers the full width of every row of the logical line.
#            `has_selection:` true|false is asserted on every row (derived from sel when omitted).
#   link:    after a `link` step: none | <url> then the span as `(R,C)-(R,C)` per row, inclusive, view-relative
#   text:    the App::selection_text value: `none` (no selection) or a quoted string with \n \t \\ \" \xNN \u{H} escapes
#   cite:    the source for every expected value; `note:` is documentation.
# PAYLOAD ESCAPES in `feed`: \xNN raw byte, \r \n \t \\, \u{H..} one scalar UTF-8 encoded.
# A `|` is NOT used for the cursor here (selection rows do not assert the screen); the feed is described in `note:`.
#
# COORDINATES: every point is (row, col), 0-based, view-relative. The core converts to absolute logical-line
# coordinates (30-core brief D-COORD). `cols` below always means the grid width of the row's `size:`.
#
# SOURCE TAGS (fetched 2026-10-31; "X does Y" means "X's source says Y": nothing was executed)
#   IT-doc   https://iterm2.com/documentation-preferences-general.html  (Selection section)
#   IT-sel   https://github.com/gnachman/iTerm2  sources/Selection/iTermSelection.m  (moveSelectionEndpointTo L571,
#            moveSelectionEndpointToAbsRange L614, scrollbackOverflowDidChange)
#   IT-word  sources/ContentAnalysis/iTermWordExtractor.m  (windowedRangeForLocation L100: class Other selects ONE
#            character; classForCharacter L560-600: Whitespace / Word / Other / Null / DoubleWidthPlaceholder)
#   IT-ext   sources/ContentAnalysis/iTermTextExtractor.m (wordSeparatorCharacterSet L52)
#   IT-pref  sources/Settings/iTermPreferences.m L748-752, L918-919 (defaults: WordCharacters "/-+\~_.",
#            CopySelection YES, TripleClickSelectsFullWrappedLines YES, DoubleClickPerformsSmartSelection NO)
#   IT-mouse sources/TerminalView/PTYMouseHandler.m (mouseDownImpl L356-430: click counts, modifiers; mouseUp L500-690)
#   IT-resize / IT-sel-clear   sources/VT100Screen/VT100ScreenMutableState+Resizing.m L121, +TerminalDelegate.m L1572/L1975
#   KT       kitty (kitty/line.c line_url_end_at, get_url_sentinel; kitty/unicode-data.h can_strip_from_end_of_url)
#   AL       alacritty_terminal/src/term/mod.rs  bounds_to_string L558, line_to_string L572
#   REND     crates/tessera-render/src/frame.rs  Selection (start/end inclusive, either order; a point on a SPACER
#            takes the whole character, an end on the WIDE half does too)
#   ADR23    docs/adr/0023-scrollback-viewport-and-scroll-anchoring.md
#   BRIEF    wave8-briefs/30-core.md (decisions D-COORD, D-CLEAR)
# =============================================================================

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A. LINEAR SELECTION BY DRAG (character granularity)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### A01_linear_forward_one_row
layer: core
size: 3x20
step: feed hello world
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,4
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,4)
has_selection: true
text: "hello"
cite: [REND] Selection ends are inclusive; [IT-sel] moveSelectionEndpointTo sets _absRange.coordRange.end = coord in Character mode
note: Cells are selected whole (decision D1 in notes: whole-cell semantics, no half-cell snapping in 0.1.0).

### A02_linear_backward_same_text
layer: core
size: 3x20
step: feed hello world
step: begin 0,4 char
step: extend 0,0
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,4)
has_selection: true
text: "hello"
cite: [REND] start/end may come in either order; [IT-sel] moveSelectionEndpointToAbsRange keeps a "flipped" live range and normalises on read
note: The core normalises to reading order in the frame; the anchor stays at (0,4) internally (see E rows for the anchor).

### A03_click_without_drag_selects_nothing
layer: core
size: 3x20
step: feed hello world
step: begin 0,3 char
sel: none
has_selection: false
text: none
cite: iTerm2 behaviour: a plain click clears the selection and creates none (zero-length live range is not a selection) [IT-sel hasSelection: needs a live range or subselections]
note: begin alone must not create a visible selection; the app calls extend on the first mouseDragged. A drag that returns to the anchor cell selects that ONE cell (A04), because whole-cell semantics make start==end a one-cell range once extend was called.

### A04_drag_inside_anchor_cell_selects_one_cell
layer: core
size: 3x20
step: feed hello world
step: begin 0,3 char
step: extend 0,3
sel: linear (0,3)-(0,3)
has_selection: true
text: "l"
cite: whole-cell semantics (D1); [REND] inclusive ends
note: AMBIGUITY: iTerm2 snaps to half-cells (drag starting in the right half of a cell begins at the next cell), so a tiny drag inside one cell selects nothing there. Recommend whole-cell for 0.1.0; the Swift side only calls extend when the pointer moved to a different cell OR left the anchor cell (gesture row G05).

### A05_linear_across_rows_hard_newlines
layer: core
size: 3x10
step: feed abc\r\ndef\r\nghi
step: begin 0,1 char
step: extend 2,1
sel: linear (0,1)-(2,1)
has_selection: true
text: "bc\ndef\ngh"
cite: [IT-doc] "a terminal newline will be copied ... when the selection includes one" (hard line ends give \n between rows); interior newline is always kept
note: Rows are separated by \n because each row ends a logical line. No trailing \n after "gh" (selection ends inside the last row).

### A06_linear_across_soft_wrap_joins_without_newline
layer: core
size: 3x5
step: feed 0123456789ab
step: begin 0,3 char
step: extend 1,2
sel: linear (0,3)-(1,2)
has_selection: true
text: "34567"
cite: [IT-doc] TripleClickSelectsFullWrappedLines treats wrapped rows as one logical line; every reference (iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm, Alacritty, xterm) joins soft-wrapped rows with no newline when copying
note: Feed wraps at col 5 (DECAWM on): row0 "01234" wrapped, row1 "56789" wrapped, row2 "ab". The selection (0,3)-(1,2) is "34" + "567" with NO newline at the wrap.

### A07_trailing_blanks_trimmed_each_line
layer: core
size: 3x10
step: feed ab\r\ncd
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 1,9
sel: linear (0,0)-(1,9)
has_selection: true
text: "ab\ncd"
cite: iTerm2 / kitty / WezTerm / Terminal.app all drop never-written trailing cells on copy; xterm copies up to the last written cell of each line [see notes: trailing-blank trimming]
note: Selection covers cells (0,2..9) and (1,2..9), which are blank; they are trimmed from each LINE (the end of a hard line), not mid-line. Decision D2: trim trailing blanks (space cells AND default-attribute empty cells) on every line end that is not a soft wrap.

### A08_blank_run_inside_line_is_kept
layer: core
size: 2x12
step: feed a   b
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,11
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,11)
has_selection: true
text: "a   b"
cite: D2: only TRAILING blanks of a hard line are trimmed; interior spaces survive
note: Tessera's Cell has no NUL state (Cell::BLANK is ' ', crates/tessera-grid/src/cell.rs), so a written trailing space and a never-written cell are the same. iTerm2 and kitty (strip_trailing_spaces=never) DO keep written trailing spaces; Tessera cannot, so it trims them. Documented deviation, see notes D2.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# B. WIDE CELLS, CLUSTERS, PAD CELLS  (cells below: `a` col0, 世 cols1-2, `b` col3)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### B01_start_on_spacer_takes_whole_character
layer: core
size: 2x10
step: feed a\u{4e16}b
step: begin 0,2 char
step: extend 0,3
sel: linear (0,2)-(0,3)
has_selection: true
text: "\u{4e16}b"
cite: [REND] "a point on the SPACER half of a wide character takes the whole character"; [AL] alacritty_terminal term/mod.rs line_to_string: "Include wide char when trailing spacer is selected" (cols.start -= 1)
note: A spacer is never a character of its own: the selection starts at the wide half. Text has no space for the spacer.

### B02_click_wide_half_extend_same_cell_selects_whole_character
layer: core
size: 2x10
step: feed a\u{4e16}b
step: begin 0,1 char
step: extend 0,1
sel: linear (0,1)-(0,1)
has_selection: true
text: "\u{4e16}"
cite: [REND] "an end on its WIDE half" takes the whole character
note: A one-cell selection on the wide half covers both cells.

### B03_end_on_spacer_includes_character
layer: core
size: 2x10
step: feed a\u{4e16}b
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,2
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,2)
has_selection: true
text: "a\u{4e16}"
cite: [REND]; [IT-word] windowedRangeForLocation: DoubleWidthPlaceholder retries at the predecessor

### B04_end_on_wide_half_includes_spacer
layer: core
size: 2x10
step: feed a\u{4e16}b
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,1
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,1)
has_selection: true
text: "a\u{4e16}"
cite: [REND] "and so does an end on its WIDE half"

### B05_combining_cluster_gives_whole_text
layer: core
size: 2x10
step: feed e\u{301}x
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,0
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,0)
has_selection: true
text: "e\u{301}"
cite: ADR 0008 (grapheme table: Cell.ch is the cluster base, the rest lives in Line::graphemes); [AL] line_to_string pushes the cell char then its zerowidth chars
note: The extraction must read the cluster from the line's grapheme table, not just Cell::ch.

### B06_zwj_emoji_cluster_wide
layer: core
size: 2x10
step: feed \u{1F468}\u{200D}\u{1F469}x
step: begin 0,1 char
step: extend 0,1
sel: linear (0,1)-(0,1)
has_selection: true
text: "\u{1F468}\u{200D}\u{1F469}"
cite: UAX29 GB11 (one cluster), unicode-width rule 1 (width 2) as in wide_grapheme_spec.txt; [REND] spacer takes the whole character
note: Cells: cluster at col 0 (WIDE|CLUSTER), spacer col 1, `x` col 2. Clicking the spacer selects the cluster.

### B07_wide_wrap_pad_cell_is_not_text
layer: core
size: 3x5
step: feed abcd\u{4e16}
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 1,1
sel: linear (0,0)-(1,1)
has_selection: true
text: "abcd\u{4e16}"
cite: crates/tessera-grid/src/cell.rs CellFlags::PAD ("padding left in the last column when a wide character wrapped"); wide_grapheme_spec.txt C01; [AL] line_to_string skips LEADING_WIDE_CHAR_SPACER
note: Row 0 is `abcd` + PAD cell (col 4, soft wrap); row 1 is 世 (cols 0-1). The PAD cell contributes no space.

### B08_cjk_double_click_selects_alnum_run_not_segmented
layer: core
size: 2x10
step: feed \u{4e16}\u{754c} x
step: begin 0,2 word
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,3)
has_selection: true
text: "\u{4e16}\u{754c}"
cite: [IT-ext] wordSeparatorCharacterSet: alphanumericCharacterSet (CJK ideographs are letters) so the pair is one run; [KT] kitty select_by_word_characters adds to "Unicode alphanumerics"
note: AMBIGUITY: iTerm2 additionally runs a language-specific tokenizer (iTermWordExtractor languageSpecificWindowedRange, NLTokenizer) that can split CJK runs into dictionary words. Recommend NO segmentation in 0.1.0: the maximal alphanumeric run is the word.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# C. WORD AND LINE GRANULARITY   WORD_CHARS = Unicode alphanumerics + the set  / - + \ ~ _ .
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### C01_double_click_word
layer: core
size: 2x20
step: feed foo bar
step: begin 0,1 word
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,2)
has_selection: true
text: "foo"
cite: [IT-word] class Word run; [IT-doc] "Double-click performs smart selection" is OFF by default so plain word selection applies [IT-pref L919]

### C02_double_click_whitespace_selects_the_run
layer: core
size: 2x20
step: feed foo  bar
step: begin 0,3 word
sel: linear (0,3)-(0,4)
has_selection: true
text: "  "
cite: [IT-word] classForCharacter: whitespace is its own class, the forward/backward search takes the whole run of that class
note: A whitespace-only selection keeps its spaces (they are not trailing: text follows).

### C03_double_click_path_uses_word_chars
layer: core
size: 2x30
step: feed cd /usr/local/bin-x_y.txt ok
step: begin 0,9 word
sel: linear (0,3)-(0,24)
has_selection: true
text: "/usr/local/bin-x_y.txt"
cite: [IT-pref L751] default WordCharacters "/-+\~_."; [IT-doc] "Adding / makes double-clicking a path select the whole path"
note: cols: `cd `=0-2, path=3-24, space=25. All of / - _ . are word characters.

### C04_double_click_other_punctuation_selects_one_character
layer: core
size: 2x20
step: feed a,b
step: begin 0,1 word
sel: linear (0,1)-(0,1)
has_selection: true
text: ","
cite: [IT-word] windowedRangeForLocation L120: "Character class is other, select one character."
note: AMBIGUITY: xterm / kitty / Alacritty select the run of non-word characters or nothing special; iTerm2 selects exactly one. Follow iTerm2 (the reference for gestures).

### C05_word_stops_at_equals_colon_at
layer: core
size: 2x30
step: feed key=value user@host a:b
step: begin 0,1 word
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,2)
has_selection: true
text: "key"
cite: [IT-pref] `= @ :` are not in "/-+\~_." so they end a word
note: DIFFERENCE: kitty's default select_by_word_characters is `@-./_~?&=%+#` (includes = @ ? & % #), Alacritty and WezTerm use boundary sets. iTerm2's set is the confirmed default; users edit it via #47.

### C06_precomposed_letters_are_word_chars
layer: core
size: 2x20
step: feed h\u{e9}llo w
step: begin 0,2 word
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,4)
has_selection: true
text: "h\u{e9}llo"
cite: [IT-ext] alphanumericCharacterSet; Unicode alphanumerics = Alphabetic + Nd/Nl/No (char::is_alphanumeric in Rust)

### C07_word_continues_across_soft_wrap
layer: core
size: 3x5
step: feed abcdefgh
step: begin 1,1 word
sel: linear (0,0)-(1,2)
has_selection: true
text: "abcdefgh"
cite: [IT-word] searchForwards/searchReverse eolBlock shouldStopEnumeratingWithCode(ignoringNewlines:NO) stops only at a hard line end; wrapped rows continue

### C08_word_stops_at_hard_line_end
layer: core
size: 3x5
step: feed abc\r\ndef
step: begin 1,0 word
sel: linear (1,0)-(1,2)
has_selection: true
text: "def"
cite: [IT-word] same eolBlock: a hard end stops the search

### C09_double_click_on_blank_area_right_of_text_selects_nothing
layer: core
size: 2x10
step: feed ab
step: begin 0,6 word
sel: none
has_selection: false
text: none
cite: [IT-word] classForCharacter returns kTextExtractorClassNull for an empty cell
note: AMBIGUITY (D4): iTerm2's Null class path is not conclusive from the source read. Recommend: a double-click past the end of the line's text selects nothing (and clears any selection), the simplest behaviour that never produces a selection with empty text.

### C10_triple_click_selects_whole_wrapped_logical_line
layer: core
size: 4x5
step: feed abcdefgh\r\nxyz
step: begin 1,2 line
sel: linear (0,0)-(1,4)
has_selection: true
text: "abcdefgh"
cite: [IT-doc] "a triple click selects a whole line, even if it was longer than one row" (TripleClickSelectsFullWrappedLines default YES [IT-pref L918]); [IT-mouse] PTYMouseHandler.m L414-420 kiTermSelectionModeWholeLine
note: Line granularity covers the full width of each row of the logical line; no trailing newline in the text (iTerm2 CopyLastNewline default NO [IT-pref L749]).

### C11_triple_click_hard_line
layer: core
size: 4x5
step: feed abcdefgh\r\nxyz
step: begin 2,0 line
sel: linear (2,0)-(2,4)
has_selection: true
text: "xyz"
cite: [IT-mouse] L414-420

### C12_triple_click_then_drag_extends_by_whole_lines
layer: core
size: 4x5
step: feed abcdefgh\r\nxyz
step: begin 0,1 line
step: extend 2,0
sel: linear (0,0)-(2,4)
has_selection: true
text: "abcdefgh\nxyz"
cite: [IT-sel] moveSelectionEndpointToAbsRange in Line/WholeLine mode moves the endpoint to the clicked line's range

### C13_double_click_drag_extends_by_whole_words
layer: core
size: 2x20
step: feed foo bar baz
step: begin 0,1 word
step: extend 0,5
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,6)
has_selection: true
text: "foo bar"
cite: [IT-sel] moveSelectionEndpointToAbsRange (word mode: endpoint = end of the word under the pointer)

### C14_double_click_drag_backwards_keeps_initial_word
layer: core
size: 2x20
step: feed foo bar baz
step: begin 0,5 word
step: extend 0,1
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,6)
has_selection: true
text: "foo bar"
cite: [IT-sel] moveSelectionEndpointToAbsRange: "range is flipped ... newRange.start = _initialAbsRange" keeps the word first double-clicked whole when dragging back over earlier words
note: The anchor is the whole initial word `bar` (cols 4-6), not a character.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# D. BLOCK (RECTANGULAR) SELECTION
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### D01_block_text_one_line_per_row_trimmed
layer: core
size: 4x10
step: feed abcdef\r\nghijkl\r\nmn\r\nopqrst
step: begin 0,1 char block
step: extend 2,3
sel: block (0,1)-(2,3)
has_selection: true
text: "bcd\nhij\nn"
cite: [IT-sel] kiTermSelectionModeBox; [AL] alacritty selection Block; every reference joins block rows with \n and trims trailing blanks of each row (kitty strip_trailing_spaces `smart` skips rectangles, `never` is its default; Tessera trims, D2)
note: Row 2 is `mn`: col 1 = `n`, cols 2-3 blank and trimmed.

### D02_block_corners_any_direction
layer: core
size: 4x10
step: feed abcdef\r\nghijkl\r\nmn\r\nopqrst
step: begin 2,3 char block
step: extend 0,1
sel: block (0,1)-(2,3)
has_selection: true
text: "bcd\nhij\nn"
cite: rectangle normalised to top-left/bottom-right; same text as D01

### D03_block_ignores_soft_wrap_each_screen_row_is_a_line
layer: core
size: 3x5
step: feed abcdefgh
step: begin 0,1 char block
step: extend 1,2
sel: block (0,1)-(1,2)
has_selection: true
text: "bc\ngh"
cite: [IT-sel] box mode selects a rectangle of cells; extraction is per screen row (no wrap joining); [KT] rectangle selection copies screen rows
note: Row 0 `abcde` (wrapped) cols 1-2 = `bc`; row 1 `fgh` cols 1-2 = `gh`. A soft wrap is NOT joined inside a block.

### D04_block_edge_cutting_wide_char_widens_that_row
layer: core
size: 3x10
step: feed a\u{4e16}b\r\nxyzw
step: begin 0,2 char block
step: extend 1,3
sel: block (0,2)-(1,3)
has_selection: true
text: "\u{4e16}b\nzw"
cite: [REND] SPACER point takes the whole character; [AL] line_to_string cols.start -= 1 on a spacer
note: Column 2 is the spacer of 世. Row 0 widens left to include the whole character; row 1 (no wide char) is just cols 2-3. The rectangle as reported stays (0,2)-(1,3); the widening is per row at extraction/render.

### D05_block_over_all_blank_rows_gives_empty_lines_trimmed_at_end
layer: core
size: 3x10
step: feed abc
step: begin 0,5 char block
step: extend 2,7
sel: block (0,5)-(2,7)
has_selection: true
text: ""
cite: D2 plus rule H03 (trailing blank lines of the whole selection are dropped)
note: A block over only blank cells is a real selection (Copy is enabled) with empty text; the app must not replace the pasteboard with an empty string (gesture row P03).

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# E. SHIFT-CLICK EXTEND (`adjust`): iTerm2 moves the endpoint NEARER the click, keeps granularity
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### E01_adjust_beyond_end_moves_end
layer: core
size: 2x20
step: feed hello world foo
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,4
step: adjust 0,10
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,10)
has_selection: true
text: "hello world"
cite: [IT-sel] beginExtendingSelectionAt "The click point is outside the live range": click after determinant.end moves the end

### E02_adjust_before_start_moves_start
layer: core
size: 2x20
step: feed hello world foo
step: begin 0,6 char
step: extend 0,10
step: adjust 0,2
sel: linear (0,2)-(0,10)
has_selection: true
text: "llo world"
cite: [IT-sel] beginExtendingSelectionAt: click before determinant.start flips and moves the start; the old end stays
note: DIFFERENCE from the 30-core brief draft ("shift-click extend keeps the anchor"): after a forward drag the anchor is the START (col 6); keeping it and flipping would give (0,2)-(0,6). iTerm2 moves the nearer endpoint and the far one stays fixed, which here is the END (col 10). Recommend iTerm2 (also xterm extend-end and Terminal.app).

### E03_adjust_inside_range_moves_nearer_endpoint
layer: core
size: 2x20
step: feed hello world foo
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,10
step: adjust 0,8
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,8)
has_selection: true
text: "hello wor"
cite: [IT-sel] beginExtendingSelectionAt "The click point is inside old live range": distanceToEnd < distanceToStart moves the end

### E04_adjust_tie_moves_start
layer: core
size: 2x20
step: feed hello world foo
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,10
step: adjust 0,5
sel: linear (0,5)-(0,10)
has_selection: true
text: " world"
cite: [IT-sel] `if (distanceToEnd < distanceToStart) move end else move start`: a tie moves the start
note: Distances are measured in cells along the logical line (VT100GridAbsCoordDistance), not in rows.

### E05_adjust_without_selection_does_nothing
layer: core
size: 2x20
step: feed hello world
step: adjust 0,4
sel: none
has_selection: false
text: none
cite: [IT-mouse] L360 `isExtension = [selection hasSelection] && shiftPressed`; without a selection a shift-click is an ordinary click (which selects nothing)

### E06_adjust_keeps_word_granularity
layer: core
size: 2x20
step: feed hello world foo
step: begin 0,0 word
step: adjust 0,8
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,10)
has_selection: true
text: "hello world"
cite: [IT-sel] beginExtendingSelectionAt: `_selectionMode = sub.selectionMode` and the clicked point is rounded with absRangeForCurrentModeAtAbsCoord (the word `world` 6-10)

### E07_adjust_keeps_line_granularity
layer: core
size: 4x10
step: feed one\r\ntwo\r\nthree
step: begin 0,1 line
step: adjust 2,0
sel: linear (0,0)-(2,9)
has_selection: true
text: "one\ntwo\nthree"
cite: [IT-sel] same; the clicked point is rounded to its logical line

### E08_adjust_keeps_block
layer: core
size: 4x10
step: feed abcdef\r\nghijkl\r\nmnopqr
step: begin 0,1 char block
step: extend 1,3
step: adjust 2,5
sel: block (0,1)-(2,5)
has_selection: true
text: "bcdef\nhijkl\nnopqr"
cite: [IT-sel] mode is kept (Box); the endpoint nearer the click (the end) moves
note: Block-mode endpoint choice by linear distance is not exercised in iTerm2's source for box mode beyond `_absRange.coordRange.end = coord`; this row asserts only the unambiguous case (click beyond both corners).

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# F. SELECT ALL
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### F01_select_all_includes_scrollback
layer: core
size: 2x5
step: feed a\r\nb\r\nc\r\nd
step: all
sel: linear (0,0)-(1,4)
has_selection: true
text: "a\nb\nc\nd"
cite: [IT-doc] Edit > Select All; every reference selects scrollback + screen on the primary screen
note: Screen shows `c`,`d`; `a`,`b` are history. `sel:` is the part inside the live view.

### F02_select_all_at_scrolled_view_clips_to_view
layer: core
size: 2x5
step: feed a\r\nb\r\nc\r\nd
step: all
step: scroll 2
sel: linear (0,0)-(1,4)
has_selection: true
text: "a\nb\nc\nd"
cite: ADR23 (the view shows the lines at the offset); selection is anchored in logical lines (D-COORD) so scrolling does not change it

### F03_select_all_drops_trailing_blank_lines
layer: core
size: 4x5
step: feed a\r\nb
step: all
has_selection: true
text: "a\nb"
cite: rule H03; iTerm2 and kitty copy no trailing blank lines (Select All over a mostly empty screen pastes the text only)
note: Without H03 the text would be "a\nb\n\n". sel not asserted (covers all rows).

### F04_select_all_on_alt_screen_is_the_alt_screen_only
layer: core
size: 2x5
step: feed a\r\nb\r\nc\x1b[?1049h\x1b[Hxy
step: all
has_selection: true
text: "xy"
cite: ADR23 ("the alternate screen has no scrollback"); the main screen is stashed

### F05_select_all_empty_terminal
layer: core
size: 2x5
step: all
has_selection: true
text: ""
cite: D4-style decision: Select All always selects; nothing to copy
note: AMBIGUITY: recommended `has_selection: true` with empty text (Select All is always enabled, Copy then writes nothing: gesture row P03).

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# G. ANCHORING AND CLEAR RULES (30-core brief D-COORD, D-CLEAR; iTerm2 differences in notes D6)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### G01_output_scrolls_selected_line_into_history_selection_survives
layer: core
size: 2x5
scrollback: 10
step: feed one\r\ntwo
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,2
step: feed \r\nthree
has_selection: true
sel: none
text: "one"
cite: ADR23 (lines entering history are tracked by Grid::scrollback_pushed; absolute logical lines do not move); [IT-sel] scrollbackOverflowDidChange keeps the range while its lines remain
note: `one` is now history line 0; the live view shows `two`/`three` so the clipped `sel:` is none.

### G02_scrolling_back_shows_the_selection
layer: core
size: 2x5
scrollback: 10
step: feed one\r\ntwo
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,2
step: feed \r\nthree
step: scroll 1
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,2)
has_selection: true
text: "one"
cite: ADR23 anchoring + D-COORD

### G03_change_of_selected_live_row_clears
layer: core
size: 3x10
step: feed hello
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,4
step: feed \rX
sel: none
has_selection: false
text: none
cite: 30-core brief D-CLEAR ("cleared on change of a selected live row")
note: DIFFERENCE from iTerm2: its source removes the selection on SD, clear screen and width change (VT100ScreenMutableState+TerminalDelegate.m L1572 terminalScrollDown, L1975 terminalClearScreen, +Resizing.m L121) and was not seen clearing on ordinary overwrites. Keeping a selection whose text silently changed makes Copy return text the user never saw, so the draft rule is kept; lead decision D6.

### G04_output_on_other_rows_keeps_selection
layer: core
size: 4x10
step: feed hello\r\nabc
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,4
step: feed \r\nz
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,4)
has_selection: true
text: "hello"
cite: D-CLEAR ("only *selected* rows changing clears it")

### G05_rewriting_identical_text_keeps_selection
layer: core
size: 3x10
step: feed hello
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,4
step: feed \rh
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,4)
has_selection: true
text: "hello"
cite: D-CLEAR compares CONTENT ("changes content"), not damage
note: AMBIGUITY (D6b): a full-screen program that repaints the same text every frame (htop, watch) would clear a damage-based rule on each repaint; content comparison avoids that. Cost: compare the selected live rows against a snapshot at each frame (only while a selection exists).

### G06_cursor_motion_alone_keeps_selection
layer: core
size: 3x10
step: feed hello
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,4
step: feed \x1b[H\x1b[2;3H
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,4)
has_selection: true
text: "hello"
cite: D-CLEAR (cursor is not row content)

### G07_history_eviction_of_a_selected_line_clears
layer: core
size: 2x5
scrollback: 2
step: feed l1\r\nl2\r\nl3\r\nl4
step: scroll 2
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,1
step: feed \r\nl5
sel: none
has_selection: false
text: none
cite: D-CLEAR ("the history evicts any selected line"); ADR23 (cap eviction)
note: History [l1,l2]; the selection is on l1; `l5` pushes l3 and evicts l1.

### G08_resize_clears
layer: core
size: 3x10
step: feed hello
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,4
step: resize 3x8
sel: none
has_selection: false
text: none
cite: D-CLEAR ("the grid resizes"); [IT-resize] iTerm2 +Resizing.m L121 removes the selection when the screen width is set destructively

### G09_alt_screen_switch_clears_both_ways
layer: core
size: 3x10
step: feed hello
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,4
step: feed \x1b[?1049h
sel: none
has_selection: false
text: none
cite: D-CLEAR ("the screen switches to/from the alternate screen")
note: The other direction is G09b.

### G09b_leaving_alt_screen_clears_selection_made_on_it
layer: core
size: 3x10
step: feed \x1b[?1049hhello
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,4
step: feed \x1b[?1049l
sel: none
has_selection: false
text: none
cite: D-CLEAR

### G10_clear_scrollback_clears
layer: core
size: 2x5
scrollback: 10
step: feed a\r\nb\r\nc
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,0
step: clear_scrollback
sel: none
has_selection: false
text: none
cite: D-CLEAR ("clear_scrollback runs"); ADR23 (clear_scrollback and ED 3 empty the history)
note: Also true when the selection was on screen rows only.

### G11_ris_clears
layer: core
size: 3x10
step: feed hello
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,4
step: feed \x1bc
sel: none
has_selection: false
text: none
cite: D-CLEAR (RIS blanks the selected row, so its content changed); ADR23 (RIS empties history)

### G12_scroll_down_over_selected_rows_clears
layer: core
size: 3x10
step: feed a\r\nb\r\nc
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 1,0
step: feed \x1b[1T
sel: none
has_selection: false
text: none
cite: [IT-sel-clear] iTerm2 terminalScrollDown calls screenRemoveSelection; here the rows' content changes so D-CLEAR applies the same way
note: SD (`CSI T`) moves row content down: selected rows 0-1 now hold different text.

### G13_output_while_scrolled_back_keeps_selection_in_view
layer: core
size: 2x5
scrollback: 10
step: feed one\r\ntwo\r\nthree
step: scroll 1
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,2
step: feed \r\nfour
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,2)
has_selection: true
text: "one"
cite: ADR23 (output while scrolled back keeps the viewed text still: the offset grows with the pushes)
note: View at scroll 1 shows `one`/`two`; after `four` the offset becomes 2 and the view still shows the same lines.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# H. TEXT EXTRACTION DETAILS
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### H01_tab_gives_spaces_not_a_tab
layer: core
size: 2x20
step: feed a\tb
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,8
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,8)
has_selection: true
text: "a       b"
cite: crates/tessera-grid keeps tab expansion as cursor motion only (cells are spaces); [AL] line_to_string reconstructs a TAB when the cell was a tab (tab_mode); iTerm2 stores TAB_FILLER and copies "\t"
note: DEVIATION (D7): iTerm2 and Alacritty copy a real tab, Tessera cannot know one was typed (cursor motion writes no cells). 7 spaces between a and b.

### H02_blank_lines_inside_selection_are_kept
layer: core
size: 4x10
step: feed a\r\n\r\nb
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 2,0
sel: linear (0,0)-(2,0)
has_selection: true
text: "a\n\nb"
cite: [AL] bounds_to_string appends \n per row; interior empty rows stay

### H03_trailing_blank_lines_of_selection_are_dropped
layer: core
size: 4x10
step: feed a
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 3,9
sel: linear (0,0)-(3,9)
has_selection: true
text: "a"
cite: [AL] bounds_to_string: `res.strip_suffix('\n')` removes ONE trailing newline; iTerm2 CopyLastNewline default NO drops the last terminal newline [IT-doc]. Tessera drops ALL trailing newlines produced by blank rows (stricter, D8) so Select All of a mostly empty screen pastes only text.

### H04_styled_blank_cells_trim_too
layer: core
size: 2x10
step: feed \x1b[41mab\x1b[K\x1b[0m
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,9
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,9)
has_selection: true
text: "ab"
cite: [IT-ext] erased cells with a background are null characters + attributes; trailing nulls are not copied

### H05_soft_wrapped_row_end_blanks_are_kept
layer: core
size: 3x5
step: feed ab   cd
step: all
has_selection: true
text: "ab   cd"
cite: [AL] line_to_string: the trailing-blank trim does not apply when the last cell has WRAPLINE; blanks at a soft wrap are interior to the logical line
note: Row 0 = `ab` + 3 spaces (soft wrap), row 1 = `cd`.

### H06_selection_ending_at_last_column_has_no_newline
layer: core
size: 3x5
step: feed hello\r\nworld
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 0,4
sel: linear (0,0)-(0,4)
has_selection: true
text: "hello"
cite: [IT-doc] CopyLastNewline default NO; [AL] strip_suffix newline
note: `hello` fills 5 columns and arms pending wrap, but the \r\n ends the line: row 0 is NOT soft-wrapped.

### H07_selection_extending_into_next_row_includes_newline
layer: core
size: 3x5
step: feed hello\r\nworld
step: begin 0,0 char
step: extend 1,0
sel: linear (0,0)-(1,0)
has_selection: true
text: "hello\nw"
cite: [AL] bounds_to_string

### H08_start_in_blank_area_gives_leading_newline
layer: core
size: 3x10
step: feed ab\r\ncd
step: begin 0,5 char
step: extend 1,0
sel: linear (0,5)-(1,0)
has_selection: true
text: "\nc"
cite: [AL] bounds_to_string: row 0 contributes "" (blank trimmed) then \n

### H09_pad_and_spacer_cells_never_emit_text
layer: core
size: 3x5
step: feed ab\u{4e16}\u{4e16}
step: all
has_selection: true
text: "ab\u{4e16}\u{4e16}"
cite: [AL] line_to_string skips WIDE_CHAR_SPACER | LEADING_WIDE_CHAR_SPACER
note: Row 0 is a b 世(cols 2-3) then a PAD cell (col 4: the second 世 needs two columns, one is left), soft-wrapped; row 1 is the second 世.

# I. LINK HIT-TESTING OVER DETECTED URLS (App::link_at, view-relative; URL detection rules in selection_spec.notes.md)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### I01_url_in_one_row
layer: core
size: 2x40
step: feed see https://example.com/a ok
step: link 0,10
link: https://example.com/a (0,4)-(0,24)
cite: notes U1-U3 / section J (scheme at a word start, URL characters to the end); kitty url_prefixes and WezTerm default rule both match `scheme://...`

### I02_cell_outside_the_url_is_none
layer: core
size: 2x40
step: feed see https://example.com/a ok
step: link 0,2
link: none
cite: section J (J34)

### I03_url_wrapped_across_rows
layer: core
size: 4x12
step: feed see https://example.com/a/b ok
step: link 1,5
link: https://example.com/a/b (0,4)-(0,11) (1,0)-(1,11) (2,0)-(2,2)
cite: notes U8; [KT] kitty extend_url / next_line_starts_with_url_chars continue a URL onto the next row; WezTerm and iTerm2 match over the logical line
note: Rows: `see https://` / `example.com/` / `a/b ok`. The span has one range per row and the hover overlay draws one Underline per range.

### I04_hard_newline_ends_url
layer: core
size: 3x20
step: feed https://exa\r\nmple.com
step: link 0,2
link: https://exa (0,0)-(0,10)
cite: notes U8 (only SOFT wraps continue a URL)

### I05_url_in_scrollback_at_scrolled_view
layer: core
size: 2x20
scrollback: 10
step: feed https://a.bc/x\r\nl2\r\nl3
step: scroll 1
step: link 0,3
link: https://a.bc/x (0,0)-(0,13)
cite: view-relative rows honour the scroll offset (30-core brief `App::link_at`)

### I06_same_cell_live_view_is_none
layer: core
size: 2x20
scrollback: 10
step: feed https://a.bc/x\r\nl2\r\nl3
step: link 0,3
link: none
cite: at offset 0 the view shows `l2`, `l3`

### I07_url_with_wide_characters
layer: core
size: 2x30
step: feed https://\u{4f8b}\u{3048}.jp/ end
step: link 0,9
link: https://\u{4f8b}\u{3048}.jp/ (0,0)-(0,15)
cite: notes U24 (non-ASCII alphanumerics are URL characters); the spacer cell (col 9) of 例 resolves to the same URL
note: Cells: `https://` 0-7, 例 8-9, え 10-11, `.jp/` 12-15.

### I08_url_after_wide_character_column_accounting
layer: core
size: 2x30
step: feed \u{4e16} https://a.bc
step: link 0,3
link: https://a.bc (0,3)-(0,14)
cite: spans are in cells, not scalars: 世 takes cols 0-1, space col 2, URL starts col 3

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# J. URL DETECTION (pure function for url.rs; rules U1-U9 in selection_spec.notes.md)
#   layer: url    input: <one logical line, \u{H} escapes, @rep(C,N)>    at: <char index>    url: <text>|none
#   span: <c0>-<c1>  inclusive CHAR indices of the URL in `input` (not cells: widths are I07/I08)
#   `at` is inside the span unless the row says otherwise. Detection never panics for any input (proptest).
#   Sources: [KT] kitty line_url_end_at / can_strip_from_end_of_url / get_url_sentinel; [WZ] wezterm default hyperlink_rules;
#   [GHT] ghostty src/config/url.zig header comment (rules 1 and 2); Tessera rules U1-U9.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

### J01_plain_url
layer: url
input: see https://example.com/a ok
at: 10
url: https://example.com/a
span: 4-24
cite: U1-U3; [KT] url_prefixes default `file ftp ftps gemini git gopher http https irc ircs kitty mailto news sftp ssh` (Tessera detects 5, D-SCHEMES)

### J02_trailing_period_is_not_part_of_the_url
layer: url
input: go to https://example.com/x.
at: 10
url: https://example.com/x
span: 6-26
cite: U4; [KT] can_strip_from_end_of_url strips trailing punctuation; [GHT] rule 1 "Do not match regexes ending with ."; [WZ] bare rule must end in `[)/a-zA-Z0-9-]`

### J03_trailing_comma
layer: url
input: see https://a.bc/x, then
at: 6
url: https://a.bc/x
span: 4-17
cite: U4; [KT]; [WZ]

### J04_closing_paren_then_period
layer: url
input: (https://a.bc/x).
at: 5
url: https://a.bc/x
span: 1-14
cite: U4+U5: strip `.` then the unbalanced `)`; [GHT] rule 2 "(https://example.com)" (do not include the parens); [WZ] rule 1 `\((\w+://\S+)\)`

### J05_balanced_parens_kept_wikipedia
layer: url
input: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo_(bar)
at: 5
url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo_(bar)
span: 0-38
cite: U5; [GHT] rule 2 "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(video_game) (include parens)"
note: kitty differs: it keeps `)` in the URL body but, when the URL is preceded by `(`, get_url_sentinel makes the first `)` the end, which truncates this URL inside parens (J06). Tessera counts balance instead.

### J06_balanced_parens_inside_surrounding_parens
layer: url
input: (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo_(bar))
at: 5
url: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo_(bar)
span: 1-39
cite: U5 (count openers and closers inside the candidate: the first `)` is balanced by `(`, the last is not and is stripped); [GHT] both cases together; kitty's sentinel rule would stop at the first `)` (documented difference)

### J07_markdown_link_target
layer: url
input: [docs](https://a.bc/x)
at: 10
url: https://a.bc/x
span: 7-20
cite: U5; [GHT] "such as in Markdown links"

### J08_square_brackets
layer: url
input: [https://a.bc/x]
at: 5
url: https://a.bc/x
span: 1-14
cite: U5 applies to `]` as to `)`; [WZ] rule 2 `\[(\w+://\S+)\]`; [KT] sentinel `]`

### J09_angle_brackets_end_the_url
layer: url
input: <https://a.bc/x>
at: 5
url: https://a.bc/x
span: 1-14
cite: U3 (`<` `>` are not URL characters); [WZ] rule 4; RFC 3986 App. C recommends `<URL>` delimiters

### J10_double_quotes_end_the_url
layer: url
input: href="https://a.bc/x"
at: 8
url: https://a.bc/x
span: 6-19
cite: U3 (`"` is not a URL character); [KT] sentinel `"`

### J11_single_quotes_trailing_trimmed
layer: url
input: 'https://a.bc/x'
at: 5
url: https://a.bc/x
span: 1-14
cite: U4 (`'` is legal inside a URL (RFC 3986) but trailing `'` is stripped); [KT] sentinel `'`

### J12_query_and_fragment_kept
layer: url
input: https://a.bc/p?q=1&r=2#f
at: 12
url: https://a.bc/p?q=1&r=2#f
span: 0-23
cite: U3; [WZ] `\S+`; [KT]

### J13_trailing_slash_kept
layer: url
input: open https://a.bc/dir/ now
at: 8
url: https://a.bc/dir/
span: 5-21
cite: U4 (`/` is never stripped); [KT] can_strip excludes `/`; [WZ] bare rule ends `[)/a-zA-Z0-9-]`

### J14_trailing_equals_ampersand_dash_kept
layer: url
input: https://a.bc/?a=&b=
at: 3
url: https://a.bc/?a=&b=
span: 0-18
cite: U4 (only . , ; : ! ? ' and " are stripped); [KT] keeps `& -` (and strips `=` only when classed as punctuation: it is a symbol)
note: AMBIGUITY: WezTerm's bare rule would drop a trailing `=` (must end in `[)/a-zA-Z0-9-]`); kitty keeps it. Recommend keep.

### J15_ipv6_host
layer: url
input: http://[::1]:8080/x
at: 8
url: http://[::1]:8080/x
span: 0-18
cite: U5 (`[` balances `]`); [GHT] ipv6_url_pattern

### J16_unbalanced_opener_is_kept
layer: url
input: https://a.bc/?q=(1
at: 3
url: https://a.bc/?q=(1
span: 0-17
cite: U5 strips only unbalanced CLOSERS; [KT] keeps `(`

### J17_empty_host_is_rejected
layer: url
input: see http:// here
at: 6
url: none
cite: U6; 30-core brief ("rejects an empty host")

### J18_empty_host_with_path_rejected
layer: url
input: http:///x
at: 3
url: none
cite: U6 (http, https, ftp need a host character right after `://`)

### J19_file_url_with_empty_host_is_a_url
layer: url
input: file:///etc/hosts
at: 8
url: file:///etc/hosts
span: 0-16
cite: U6 (file allows an empty host); [GIST] "file://... the hostname ... empty counts as local"

### J20_file_url_with_host
layer: url
input: file://localhost/etc/hosts
at: 12
url: file://localhost/etc/hosts
span: 0-25
cite: U6; the allowlist (local host only) is applied at OPEN time (30-app D-OPEN), not here

### J21_mailto
layer: url
input: mail mailto:a@b.co now
at: 8
url: mailto:a@b.co
span: 5-17
cite: U7; [KT] url_prefixes includes mailto; [GHT] `mailto:`

### J22_mailto_without_address_rejected
layer: url
input: mailto: and mailto:nobody
at: 2
url: none
cite: U7 (the part after `mailto:` needs `@` with text on both sides)

### J23_bare_email_is_not_a_link
layer: url
input: write to a@b.co please
at: 10
url: none
cite: U7; DIFFERENCE: [WZ] default rule 6 and iTerm2 smart selection link bare emails; 0.1.0 does not (decision D14)

### J24_ftp_with_credentials
layer: url
input: ftp://u:p@h.io/f.txt
at: 10
url: ftp://u:p@h.io/f.txt
span: 0-19
cite: U1-U3 (`@` and `:` are URL characters)

### J25_scheme_is_case_insensitive_url_kept_as_typed
layer: url
input: HTTP://A.BC/X
at: 4
url: HTTP://A.BC/X
span: 0-12
cite: RFC 3986 3.1 ("schemes are case-insensitive"); the text is returned as typed

### J26_scheme_must_start_a_word
layer: url
input: xhttp://a.bc
at: 6
url: none
cite: U1 (the scheme must not be preceded by an alphanumeric, `+`, `-` or `.`); avoids linking inside identifiers

### J27_unsupported_schemes_are_not_detected
layer: url
input: ssh://host/x git://h/x javascript:alert(1) tel:123
at: 3
url: none
cite: D-SCHEMES (30-core brief): detection covers http, https, ftp, file, mailto only; kitty/Ghostty also detect ssh/git/tel/magnet/... and are NOT followed

### J28_two_urls_on_a_line
layer: url
input: https://a.bc/x https://d.ef/y
at: 20
url: https://d.ef/y
span: 15-28
cite: U3 (whitespace ends a URL)

### J29_ideographic_full_stop_ends_url
layer: url
input: https://a.bc/x\u{3002}next
at: 5
url: https://a.bc/x
span: 0-13
cite: U3: `U+3002` is neither alphanumeric nor in the URL character set

### J30_non_ascii_letters_are_url_characters
layer: url
input: https://\u{4f8b}\u{3048}.jp/
at: 9
url: https://\u{4f8b}\u{3048}.jp/
span: 0-13
cite: U3 (non-ASCII alphanumerics allowed: IRIs); [GHT] `\w` is Unicode-aware

### J31_ellipsis_strips_all_dots
layer: url
input: see https://a.bc/x...
at: 5
url: https://a.bc/x
span: 4-17
cite: U4 (strip repeatedly)

### J32_trailing_colon_stripped_port_kept
layer: url
input: https://a.bc: https://d.ef:8080/z
at: 5
url: https://a.bc
span: 0-11
cite: U4; [GHT] no_trailing_colon

### J33_url_inside_html_attribute
layer: url
input: <a href="https://a.bc/x">
at: 12
url: https://a.bc/x
span: 9-22
cite: U3 (`"` and `>` end it)

### J34_trimmed_punctuation_cell_is_not_part_of_the_link
layer: url
input: see https://a.bc/x.
at: 18
url: none
cite: U4: the stripped `.` is outside the span (hover underline stops before it)

### J35_length_cap_accepts_2083_chars
layer: url
input: https://a.bc/@rep(a,2070)
at: 100
url: https://a.bc/@rep(a,2070)
span: 0-2082
cite: U9; the OSC 8 cap [GIST] "Both VTE and iTerm2 limit the URI to 2083 bytes"
note: AMBIGUITY (D15): bounding detection keeps the per-hover cost constant on a line of one huge token. Recommend the same 2083-char cap.

### J36_length_over_cap_is_not_a_link
layer: url
input: https://a.bc/@rep(a,2071)
at: 100
url: none
cite: U9

### J37_scheme_alone_is_not_a_link
layer: url
input: use https:// here and http:
at: 6
url: none
cite: U6 (`https://` with nothing after it)
